pumac-2021-geometry-a-07.title: $P$ is the foot from $A$ onto $HM$
pumac-2021-geometry-a-07.body:
Let $H$ be the orthocenter and $M$ the midpoint of $BC$. The circle $AEF$ has diameter $AH$, so $\angle APH=90^\circ$. If $A'$ is the antipode of $A$ on the circumcircle, then $\angle APA'=90^\circ$ as well, hence $P,H,A'$ are collinear. Since $BHCA'$ is a parallelogram, $M$ is the midpoint of $HA'$, so $P$ lies on line $HM$ and $AP\perp HM$: $AP$ is the distance from $A$ to line $HM$.

Coordinates: $B=(0,0)$, $C=(20,0)$, $A=(7,2\sqrt{30})$ (since $x=\frac{169+400-289}{40}=7$). $H=(7,y_H)$ with $BH\perp AC$: $7\cdot13-2\sqrt{30}\,y_H=0$, so $y_H=\frac{91}{2\sqrt{30}}$. $M=(10,0)$.

$\vec{MH}=\left(-3,\frac{91}{2\sqrt{30}}\right)$, $|MH|^2=9+\frac{8281}{120}=\frac{9361}{120}$, and $\vec{MA}=(-3,2\sqrt{30})$. The cross product is $(-3)\frac{91}{2\sqrt{30}}+3\cdot2\sqrt{30}=\frac{87}{2\sqrt{30}}$. Hence
$$AP=\frac{87/(2\sqrt{30})}{\sqrt{9361/120}}=\frac{87}{\sqrt{9361}}=\frac{87\sqrt{9361}}{9361}.$$
Here $9361=11\cdot23\cdot37$ is square-free and $\gcd(87,9361)=1$, so $a=87$.

**Answer: 87**

pumac-2021-geometry-a-08.title: Signed distances to the bisector
pumac-2021-geometry-a-08.body:
Let $s=\frac{7+12+10}2=\frac{29}2$. Then $AE=AF=s-12=\frac52$, $BD=s-10=\frac92$, $DC=s-7=\frac{15}2$ for the touch point $D$ on $BC$.

By Menelaus on $\triangle ABC$ with line $EFX$: $\frac{AF}{FB}\cdot\frac{BX}{XC}\cdot\frac{CE}{EA}=1$ with $FB=\frac92$, $CE=\frac{15}2$ gives $\frac{BX}{XC}=\frac35$ (external division), so $X=\frac{5B-3C}2$.

$AE=AF$ means the bisector $\ell$ of $\angle A$ is the perpendicular bisector of $EF$, so $\ell\perp EF$. Let $\sigma(P)$ be the signed distance from $P$ to $\ell$ (positive on the $AC$ side); it is an affine function. With $\phi=\frac A2$: $\sigma(E)=\frac52\sin\phi$, $\sigma(B)=-7\sin\phi$, $\sigma(C)=10\sin\phi$. Then $\sigma(X)=\frac{5(-7)-3(10)}{2}\sin\phi=-\frac{65}2\sin\phi$ and for the midpoint $N$ of $EX$: $\sigma(N)=\frac12\left(\frac52-\frac{65}2\right)\sin\phi=-15\sin\phi$.

The bisector meets segment $NC$ at $P$ with $NP:PC=|\sigma(N)|:|\sigma(C)|=15:10=3:2$. So $a+b=5$.

**Answer: 5**

pumac-2021-geometry-a-08.title: Coordinate check
pumac-2021-geometry-a-08.body:
Placing $B=(0,0)$, $C=(12,0)$ and computing $E,X,N$ and the bisector explicitly gives $NP/PC=1.5$, i.e. $3:2$.

**Answer: 5**
